PG001.name: Hardcoded Password
PG001.description: Credentials stored directly in source code can be exposed.
PG001.recommendation: Use environment variables or a secrets manager.

PG002.name: Dangerous eval Usage
PG002.recommendation: Avoid eval() and use safer parsing methods.

PG003.name: Hardcoded Secret
PG003.description: Sensitive secrets such as API keys or tokens stored in source code can be exposed.
PG003.recommendation: Use environment variables or a dedicated secrets manager.

PG004.name: SQL Injection Risk
PG004.description: User-controlled data combined directly with SQL queries can allow attackers to manipulate database commands.
PG004.recommendation: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements.

PG005.name: Command Injection
PG005.description: Unsafely executing system commands can allow attacker-controlled input to execute arbitrary operating-system commands.
PG005.recommendation: Avoid shell execution with untrusted input. Use safe subprocess APIs with argument lists and validate inputs.

PG006.name: Path Traversal
PG006.description: File operations built from user-controlled paths can escape the intended directory and read or modify arbitrary files.
PG006.recommendation: Resolve the constructed path and verify it stays inside a trusted base directory before opening it.

PG007.name: Cross-Site Scripting
PG007.description: Unescaped user input reflected into an HTTP response body allows attackers to run scripts in the victim's browser.
PG007.recommendation: Escape user-controlled values with markupsafe.escape before placing them in a response.

PG008.name: Open Redirect
PG008.description: Redirects to user-supplied destinations can send victims to attacker-controlled sites.
PG008.recommendation: Restrict redirect targets to relative paths starting with a single slash.

PG009.name: SSRF
PG009.description: Outbound requests built from user-controlled URLs can reach internal services, cloud metadata endpoints, or arbitrary hosts.
PG009.recommendation: Validate the destination against a strict allowlist of trusted hosts or URL prefixes before making the request; block non-HTTP schemes and private/internal addresses.

PG010.name: Insecure Deserialization
PG010.description: Deserializing attacker-controlled data with pickle or dill can reconstruct arbitrary objects and execute attacker-chosen code through the __reduce__ mechanism.
PG010.recommendation: Do not deserialize untrusted data with pickle or dill. Use a data-only format such as JSON, or restrict deserialization to a RestrictedUnpickler subclass whose find_class only permits explicitly allowlisted modules.
